items.rationale: Necessary dismantling and refitting in the affected cellar is covered under §5.2.6 or §5.2.7. Case 46 supports €90 for one service, provided it is not already included in the dryer charge.
Section 5.2.7 covers drying for the period supported by moisture readings. The seven billed days fit within the reported drying period and support a gross threshold of €313.
Section 7.4.4 requires an itemised list, which is not provided. The €39 estimate applies only if required materials are subsequently documented and are not already included in another charge.
Sections 5.2.6 and 7.14(c) allow necessary reinstatement with a mineral-wool shell of the original diameter. The comparable one-piece allowance is €26.
Sections 5.2.1 and 3.5(d) allow the first charge for disposal of the same debris. This first-listed charge is estimated at €60 for the small volume of cellar waste.
Section 5.2.6 covers levelling the affected substrate as part of making good. The comparable single material charge is €38.

Section 5.2.6 covers necessary preparation of the affected wall, but §§3.5(d) and 7.4.1 bar overlap with levelling, removal or separately billed labour. If this is distinct work, 2.78 m² at about €30/m² gives €83 gross.
Section 5.2.6 expressly covers a necessary service opening to access the damaged element. The comparable single opening in Case 46 supports €19 gross.

The tiles meet the 90 × 90 cm limit in §7.14(d), subject to like-kind reinstatement under §7.1.6. Five tiles provide 4.05 m² including cuts and offcuts; at about €52/m², the gross materials threshold is €211.

The billed format exceeds §7.14(d), and §3.5(f) bars partial payment for a line outside the standard threshold. If accepted exceptionally on a standard-equivalent basis, the conditional allowance would be about €211 for the affected area, not a designer-tile price.
Sections 5.2.6 and 7.14(a) cover standard sanitary silicone joints needed to finish the affected tiling. At about €13/m, the gross threshold is €47.
Section 7.4.2 allows one travel charge per contractor per document, and this is the only tiling travel line. The gross threshold is €81.
Section 7.4.1 covers necessary labour at customary rates, excluding hours already included in unit or lump-sum prices. The comparable 14-hour threshold is €1,239 gross if the hours are distinct.

Section 5.2.6 covers necessary removal in the affected basement, and the line identifies both materials. Comparable removal charges support about €90 gross, excluding any disposal already billed under item 5.
Sections 5.2.6 and 7.1.5 cover removal of affected plaster in the basement only. The single billed unit supports a gross threshold of €29.

Section 3.5(b) excludes work outside the documented damage area, and the attic work is expressly unrelated. The €29 conditional estimate reflects a comparable single removal unit, not a payable amount.

Sections 5.2.1 and 3.5(d) exclude the second charge for the same disposal, even across contractors. The €60 conditional estimate would apply only if this were documented as a distinct disposal charge.
